text: One does not become enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making the darkness conscious.
citation: C. G. Jung, “The Philosophical Tree”, Alchemical Studies (CW 13), §335
label: Open quote source notes

text: The psychological rule says that when an inner situation is not made conscious, it happens outside, as fate.
citation: C. G. Jung, “Christ, a Symbol of the Self”, Aion (CW 9ii), §126
label: Open quote source notes

text: Everyone knows nowadays that people “have complexes.” What is not so well known, though far more important theoretically, is that complexes can have us.
citation: C. G. Jung, “A Review of the Complex Theory”, CW 8, §200
label: Open quote source notes

text: Individuation does not shut one out from the world, but gathers the world to itself.
citation: C. G. Jung, “On the Nature of the Psyche”, CW 8, §432
label: Open quote source notes

text: The goal is important only as an idea; the essential thing is the opus which leads to the goal: that is the goal of a lifetime.
citation: C. G. Jung, “The Psychology of the Transference”, CW 16, §400
label: Open quote source notes

text: The bigger the crowd, the more negligible the individual.
citation: C. G. Jung, The Undiscovered Self (CW 10), p. 14
label: Open quote source notes
